01 · The idea

Look launched, not generated.

MuzMesh is the design partner for AI startups. Brand, landing page and launch kit, designed by people, ready in five days. Our own brand has to prove the point: if it looks like a prompt, nobody believes the pitch.

One accentBlack, bone and one orange.

Orange is a signal, not a mood. It marks the one thing to press, the bullet on a label, a live dot. Everything else is black and off-white.

Show the workReal artifacts beat effects.

We show build logs, browser windows, tickets and finished pages. No glowing orbs, no gradients on text, no sparkle icon.

Launch languageA launch, told like one.

Mono labels, a five-day countdown, a launch pass with IDEA → LIVE. The vocabulary of shipping, set calmly.

One typefaceInter Tight for everything.

Character comes from weight, spacing and the two-tone headline, never from a second display font. Mono is for data only.

Personality: considered, plain-spoken, quietly confident, founder-to-founder. We sound like the designer you’d hire, not the agency pitch deck.

02 · Logo

A wordmark, set in our own type.

The logo is the word muzmesh, lowercase, Inter Tight Bold at −1.5% tracking, outlined so it renders the same everywhere. The avatar is the m with an orange square full stop, the same square that leads every label.

Primary · bone on blackmuzmesh-wordmark-light.svg
Ink on papermuzmesh-wordmark.svg
Ink on orange · raresame file
xx
Clear space = x, the height of the “m”min width 72px
muzmesh-avatar.svg · muzmesh-favicon.svgLinkedIn, X, Fiverr, favicon

Do

  • Use the SVG files. Never retype the wordmark in a design tool.
  • Bone (#F4F4F1) on black, ink on paper or orange. Nothing else.
  • Let the giant cropped wordmark close a page (the footer), in stone grey.
  • In the nav, the 22px live-text version is fine: same font, same tracking.

Don’t

  • Colour the wordmark orange, or put a gradient, glow or outline on it.
  • Add a sparkle, spark or any “AI” symbol next to it.
  • Capitalise it in the logo. In running text, write MuzMesh.
  • Stretch, rotate or re-track it, or set it smaller than 72px wide.

Status: this wordmark is the working logo until a custom-drawn mark is commissioned. The files are named so a future logo can replace them without touching any page.

03 · Colour

Black, bone and one signal.

Two themes share one orange. Launch is the default for the website, social and decks. Paper is for proposals, invoices, legal pages, long reads and anything printed.

Do

  • One orange button per view. Everything else is bone, ghost or a link.
  • Dark text (#0E0E10) on orange, always. Hover goes lighter (#FF6A20).
  • On paper, orange text uses signal-ink #B33A06.
  • Use the dim grey for the first half of a two-tone headline.

Don’t

  • White text on orange (3.4:1, fails).
  • Orange text on paper at #F2580F (3.0:1, fails).
  • Purple, blue or multi-stop gradients. Those are the “AI slop” look we sell against.
  • Orange backgrounds behind whole sections.
04 · Type

One sans. One mono. That’s all.

Inter Tight carries every word. JetBrains Mono is reserved for labels, numbers in logs, timestamps and code. Both load free from Google Fonts.

Inter Tight · 400 500 600 700
Aa
RegularMediumSemiboldBoldItalic
JetBrains Mono · 400 500
00:15
READY IN 15 SECONDSLAUNCH PASS
{{TYPE_ROWS}}

Do

  • Headlines at weight 500 with tight negative tracking. Calm, not shouty.
  • Split a headline into setup (dim) and payoff (full colour).
  • Mono labels in uppercase with the 5px orange square in front.
  • text-wrap: balance on headlines, tabular-nums on figures.

Don’t

  • Bold (700) headlines, all-caps headlines, or italics for emphasis in headlines.
  • Mono for paragraphs or buttons.
  • Bricolage Grotesque, Instrument Serif or Newsreader for MuzMesh. They appear on the homepage only inside the example client brands, to show range.
  • Body text under 13px, or lines wider than about 65 characters.
05 · Iconography

Thin lines, drawn on one grid.

Icons are quiet line drawings that match Inter Tight’s stroke. They label and point; they never decorate. The set covers what our pages and posts need today, and new icons follow the same grid.

{{ICON_GRID}}
162px safe areastroke 1.6 · round
Grid16 × 16, 2px safe area. Draw inside 12 × 12.
Stroke1.6 at 16 and 20px, 1.4 at 24px and up. Round caps and joins. No fills.
ColourcurrentColor: icons take the text colour. Orange only when the icon is the signal (a check in a kit list).
Sizes16 in buttons and lists, 20 in nav and cards, 24 for feature rows. Never above 32.

3 · Texture

Dotted workbench · 24px
Copper light curtain · hero only
Grain · 5% on full-bleed dark

Do

  • Photograph real work sessions, sketches, Figma files and the people doing them.
  • Crop tight on hands and faces; leave dark space for type on the side.
  • Use one grade per layout: all natural or all duotone.
  • Credit stock photos in docs/brand/imagery/SOURCES.md and swap them for our own when we have them.

Don’t

  • Put text over busy parts of a photo, or over a photo without the dark gradient.
  • Tint photos orange. Orange stays for signals.
  • Use device mockups with fake UI or invented client logos.
  • Use illustrations of people, mascots or abstract 3D shapes.

09 · Layout and space

Wide frame, narrow content.

The nav runs to a 1640px frame; section content stops at 1120px. Sections breathe: 96 to 160px above, 96 to 140px below, with a hairline between them.

Space · 4px base
{{SPACE_ROWS}}
Radius
{{RADIUS_ROWS}}
{{LAYOUT_ROWS}}
Layout tokenValueUse

Section pattern: quiet label, two-tone H2, then a 400px lead column to the right on desktop (.mm-split), stacking under 900px. Cards and benches sit 56px below the header. Use hairlines (--mm-hair) between rows instead of boxes where you can.

10 · Motion

One story, scrubbed by scroll.

The homepage is a single timeline you scroll through: build, launch, get lost, get found. Everything else moves quietly.

{{MOTION_ROWS}}
TokenValueUse

Do

  • Animate transform and opacity only.
  • Lift buttons 1px on hover; one pulse ring on the main CTA at most.
  • Honour reduced motion: jump to the end state, no autoplay.

Don’t

  • Animate filters, blurs, box-shadows or background positions on large areas.
  • Glow pulses, shimmer text, typing cursors on headlines.
  • Fade sections in from nothing on scroll: content is visible at rest.
11 · Voice and copy

Say it plainly. Then stop.

We write like a founder talking to a founder: short sentences, real numbers, no hype. The reader should finish a section knowing exactly what they get and what it costs.

HeadlinesSetup, then payoff.

“A website is one page of your launch. We design the rest.” “One price. No surprises.”

ButtonsSay what happens.

“Plan my launch”, “See what’s included”, “Build my idea”. First person on the main CTA. Never “Get started” or “Learn more”.

NumbersExact and true.

“$500 to set up, $200 a month.” “Live in five business days.” No invented stats, testimonials, client logos or “10x”.

Words we uselaunch · kit · pass · founder · live · yours

Words we avoid: revolutionary, unlock, seamless, supercharge, cutting-edge, AI-powered, game-changer, and emoji.

Write

  • A designer draws your logo, sets your brand and designs your page in Figma.
  • We shape and edit your words, but we don’t write them from scratch.
  • Need more pages? We’ll quote it before we start, never after.

Not

  • Unlock your startup’s full potential with our AI-powered branding.
  • We craft pixel-perfect, world-class experiences ✨
  • 90% of startups fail because of bad design. (unsupported)

Names and spelling: MuzMesh in text, muzmesh in the logo, MuzMesh Creative for the legal name and footer. Five days in copy, “5 days” in labels and the pass. Curly quotes and apostrophes. Sentence case everywhere except mono labels.

15 · Audit and open items

What we checked, what we changed.

The guideline was audited against the homepage stylesheet (web/src/styles/home.css) and the rest of the site. These are the gaps found, how they were settled, and what still needs a decision.

FixedTwo hover colours for the orange button. The nav pill went darker (#CC3D08, 3.9:1 with dark text, fails) while the big CTAs went lighter (#FF6A20). Hover is now always lighter.
FixedFaint text below AA on panels. 50% bone measured 4.5:1 on raised panels. Faint is now 56% (6.0:1).
FixedTicket small print at 4.0:1. Paper labels now use #595857 (6.2:1) instead of 58% ink.
FixedOrange text on light pages failed. Added signal-ink #B33A06 (5.2:1 on paper, 6.0:1 under white text). The older site pages now use it in place of the indigo placeholder.
FixedTwo eyebrow styles. Some sections used spaced Inter Tight caps, others mono. The rule is now mono for every label; the quiet variant drops the square.
FixedOne-off colours. Footer grey, the dim headline grey and the form error colours now have names (stone, ash, danger) instead of loose hex values.
FixedDots vs squares. Rule written down: a square marks a label or list item, a circle marks something live or a position.
FixedRetired v1. Yellow #FFD60A, Archivo and the paper-first layout are archived. The four hero test palettes (Oxblood, Teal, Magenta, Green) were explorations for an earlier hero and are not part of the brand.
AddedIconography and imagery. v2 first shipped without them. There is now a 28-icon set on one grid, a photo grade (natural and duotone), texture rules and visual do/don’t examples.
AddedSocial kit. Profiles, banner safe zones, feed rhythm, a carousel structure, story safe zones, a caption template and a size table for every platform we use.
Follow-upPoint home.css at the tokens. Once the homepage PR is merged, its local --y, --fg and --raise variables can read from tokens.css. Values already match, apart from the hover and faint fixes above.
OpenOur own photos. The example photos are stock (credited). Shoot a few real work sessions to replace them.
OpenCustom logo. The outlined wordmark and “m.” avatar are the working logo. Commission a drawn mark later, or keep this one.
Open“Designed by people” or “human-led, AI-assisted”. The homepage says the first. Pick one and use it everywhere.
